source_name: CBCG Radna studija br. 10 — Analiza finansijskog tržišta u Crnoj Gori (PDF exemplar)
why_relevant: Concrete exemplar of the CBCG working-paper PDF pattern; useful to pin the URL template (/slike_i_fajlovi/fajlovi/fajlovi_publikacije/radne_studije/<slug>.pdf) for systematic harvesting of the whole series.

source_name: CBCG — Godišnji finansijski iskazi Centralne banke Crne Gore
why_relevant: Audited annual financial statements of the central bank itself. Secondary for market statistics but the authoritative record of CBCG's own balance sheet, currency-in-circulation-related items and payment-system revenue, useful as a cross-check on cash-usage and payment-system throughput narratives.

source_name: CBCG — Odluka o izvještajima koji se dostavljaju CBCG o platnom prometu (BUPPK reporting decision + annexes)
why_relevant: The reporting decision and its annex forms define exactly which cash/ATM/POS fields payment service providers must report quarterly (e.g. BUPPK — number of acceptance devices such as ATMs and POS terminals; separate lines for ATM cash withdrawals and cash deposits). This is the schema key that makes the published ZIP datasets interpretable, and it reveals fields that exist but are not published.

source_name: Zakon o platnom prometu Crne Gore — consolidated text (CBCG PDF)
why_relevant: The statute that defines what a payment institution and an e-money institution are, which activities require a licence, and which reporting obligations generate the public statistics. PSD2-aligned amendments (in force 8 October, per reporting) introduced account information services and payment initiation services as licensable categories — the legal basis for the AISP/PISP entries visible in the register. Essential for interpreting register categories correctly.

source_name: UBCG — Pregled rada za 2024. godinu (annual activity report)
why_relevant: Annual self-report of association activity: committee work (payment systems, cards, SEPA, security), projects, and sector positions. Useful for tracking which payment/card topics the industry is actively working on and who represents whom.

source_name: UBCG — Statut 2025 (association statute)
why_relevant: The 2025/2026 statute defines 11 expert committees with mandates, annual work plans and reporting duties — i.e. it tells you what documents the association is obliged to generate and therefore what can be requested or expected to appear.

source_name: Infintech conference (Tivat, organised by Logate) - agenda and participants
why_relevant: Recurring regional ME fintech/banking conference (nine panels in 2025 on digital transformation, AI, embedded finance, future of banking) organised by Montenegrin IT firm Logate. Its agenda and delegate/sponsor list is the single densest annual snapshot of who sells payments technology into Montenegro.

source_name: International bank-of-the-year awards coverage for Montenegro (Global Finance / Euromoney / The Banker, as reported by ME media)
why_relevant: Annual 'best bank in Montenegro' awards from Global Finance, Euromoney and The Banker, reported locally with supporting figures (e.g. asset size and lending market share cited for CKB). The award write-ups leak balance-sheet and market-share numbers and signal which institutions are investing in digital/card channels.

source_name: Bankar.me pricing/fee journalism (e.g. cost of instant payments in Montenegro)
why_relevant: Sector media periodically compiles cross-bank fee comparisons (instant payments, card fees, ATM withdrawals) in a readable table form, sometimes ahead of or more granularly than the regulator's own comparison pages, and flags pricing moves worth investigating.

source_name: IMF FAS annual results press release / Highlights report
why_relevant: Announces each annual FAS vintage, its coverage changes and new series (POS pilot disaggregated rural/urban, fintech lending, gender splits). Best trigger signal for a refresh of the Montenegro FAS pull and for knowing which new indicators became available.

source_name: IMF Country Report No. 25/304 — Montenegro 2025 Article IV Consultation
why_relevant: Most recent full staff report; contains banking-sector soundness tables, credit and deposit aggregates, and macro-financial context (growth 3.2% 2024/H1-2025, inflation 4.9% Sept 2025) plus EU-accession-2028 framing that drives payments-modernisation policy.

source_name: World Bank / IMF FSAP Montenegro — Technical Note on Financial Infrastructure
why_relevant: Independent structural assessment of the Montenegrin payment infrastructure: the RTGS/DNS design, the EUR 1,000 threshold rule, the interoperable ATM/POS network routed through international card schemes, and the dominance of cash in retail payments. Gives the analytical frame the CBCG tables lack, though the vintage means the IPS/SEPA developments are not covered.

source_name: World Bank — Montenegro FSAP Technical Note & CPSS/CGPSS retail payments assessments
why_relevant: Independent assessment of Montenegro's retail payments and card infrastructure; notably flags data gaps (e.g. no published count of ACTIVE debit/credit cards, and a recommendation to collect ATM/PoS downtime data) — directly calibrates how much the CBCG card series can be trusted for adoption analysis.

source_name: CKB — audited consolidated financial statements 2024 (PDF)
why_relevant: Concrete PDF instance of the market leader's audited statements; notes typically carry fee-and-commission income splits that proxy card/acquiring volumes.

source_name: EPC List of SEPA Scheme Countries (EPC409-09)
why_relevant: Versioned authoritative list defining which countries/territories are in SEPA geographical scope; the version history is a clean machine-trackable record of Montenegro's status change.

source_name: MINA / CdM / Antena M / Aktuelno — Montenegrin business press relaying monthly CBCG payment-traffic releases
why_relevant: These outlets republish the CBCG monthly payment-traffic figures within days, in a consistent sentence template. Useful as a redundancy channel when the CBCG page is restructured or a monthly release is missed, and as a timestamped record of what was published when.

entity_name: EBRD Montenegro country strategy & project/news pages
source_name: EBRD Montenegro Country Diagnostic — Private investment challenges and opportunities
why_relevant: Structural diagnostic of Montenegro's private and financial sector; the diagnostic series (see Serbia/North Macedonia peers) covers access to finance, banking-sector structure and digitalisation constraints relevant to payments/POS adoption.

source_name: ECB — Governing Council decisions and MIP news on non-euro-area/Western Balkans TIPS access
why_relevant: The 7 June 2024 Governing Council decision authorising the TIPS clone for Montenegro, Kosovo, North Macedonia, BiH and Albania is the formal regulatory approval underpinning the instant-payments agenda; ECB MIP news and speeches add cross-border payments strategy context.

source_name: EC Screening Report Montenegro — Chapter 4 Free Movement of Capital
why_relevant: Baseline structural description of Montenegro's payment/capital regime at screening (2013); useful as the historical benchmark against which later progress reports and closing benchmarks are measured.

source_name: Adriatic Bank — Mastercard membership and Apple Pay launch announcements
why_relevant: Bank-side announcements co-authored with the scheme: a new acquiring AND issuing Mastercard principal member in ME (a rare, datable change in the ME acquiring market structure) and a first Apple Pay rollout. Scheme-milestone news often appears on the issuer site before, or instead of, the scheme's own newsroom.

source_name: BIS Central Bankers' Speeches — CBCG governor/vice-governor speeches on instant payments
why_relevant: CBCG leadership speeches archived by BIS give quantified, forward-looking statements about the instant-payment rollout, fraud/AML controls and volumes that predate the statistical releases. An example is the speech at the regional conference on AML/CFT and anti-fraud procedures for instant payments.

source_name: CDM.me — republication of MasterIndex Crna Gora findings
why_relevant: Mainstream ME news portal that republishes MasterIndex results with headline percentages. Serves as a redundancy/backup channel if the Mastercard country page is restructured or an edition is delisted, and often carries figures in a plain-text form easier to extract than the scheme's own layout.

source_name: EU Delegation to Montenegro (EEAS) — SEPA operational-membership communications
why_relevant: EU-side confirmation and framing of Montenegro's operational entry into SEPA, published in Montenegrin. Useful for dating the milestone independently of CBCG and for linking payments integration to the accession agenda, which drives future reporting obligations.

source_name: Program pristupanja Crne Gore EU (PPCG) 2025–2026 — Ministry of European Affairs
why_relevant: The national accession programme sets dated, forward-looking commitments per chapter, including payment-system legislation, SEPA and instant-payments deliverables — forward targets no domestic statistical publisher produces.

source_name: Prva banka Crne Gore — bond prospectus filings on SCMN (Komisija za tržište kapitala)
why_relevant: Bond prospectuses are the richest bank-level disclosure format in Montenegro: business description typically includes client counts, card portfolio, branch/ATM network and channel strategy at a granularity annual reports omit.

source_name: Visa 'Visa Pulse' regional consumer payment-habits research (Montenegro cut)
why_relevant: Scheme-commissioned consumer survey with Montenegro-specific figures (e.g. share of citizens buying online, share using smartphone as primary payment method) — exactly the cash-preference/digital-adoption metrics missing from official statistics. Full report is corporate; press coverage carries the numbers.

source_name: UNDP Montenegro — Procjena regulatornog okvira za razvoj FinTech industrije u Crnoj Gori
why_relevant: Donor-funded assessment of Montenegro's fintech regulatory framework — the kind of document that names the actual market participants, quantifies barriers to e-money and payment licensing, and explains why the e-money register is empty. Provides baseline context and a likely bibliography of further local sources. Dated 2022, so treat figures as historical.

source_name: Payten d.o.o. Podgorica — Montenegro legal entity (contact/recruitment footprint)
why_relevant: Confirms Payten operates a registered Montenegrin subsidiary (Serdara Jola Piletića 3A, Podgorica; asseco-see.me email domain) and its job ads (ATM/POS field-maintenance subcontractors, ATM deployment coordinators) are a proxy signal for estate size and expansion. Hiring pattern is an indirect read on terminal fleet growth. Also points to the legacy asseco-see.me domain as a further target.

source_name: Adria TV / Preduzetnica — instant-payment uptake reporting (CBCG statements)
why_relevant: Carries CBCG-sourced claims about instant-payment adoption dynamics (reported five-fold growth in transaction counts and changing consumer habits) at a granularity earlier than the quarterly tables. Treat the figures as attributed claims to be confirmed against the IPS statistics page.

source_name: Alta Pay Group d.o.o. Podgorica — Montenegro operation (Alta Pay / AltaPay group)
why_relevant: Licensed payment institution (founded Podgorica, October 2019) running a bill-payment point network across Montenegro: EPCG electricity, internet and cable TV, Ministry of Interior fees, CRPS fees, cadastre, residence tax and school fees, plus payments for legal entities. Group-level communications report revenue multiples and expansion, and the group is linked to Alta banka — making it the clearest case of a payment institution converging on banking. The Montenegro-facing presence is partly on Facebook rather than a dedicated .me site, which weakens machine-collectability.

source_name: CEE Legal Matters briefing — 'SEPA in Montenegro: Benefits and Challenges'
why_relevant: Practitioner legal briefing dating the SEPA adherence steps of Montenegrin banks (all banks approved by 13 June 2025; operational use from 6 Oct 2025) — useful corroboration of the EPC register timeline from a professional-services vantage point.

entity_name: Council of the EU / Accession Conference press releases on Montenegro chapter closures
source_name: Council of the EU / Accession Conference press releases on Montenegro chapter closures
why_relevant: Records the formal opening/closing of Chapter 4 and associated closing benchmarks — the regulatory milestones that drive payment-market modernisation deadlines. Chapter 4 provisionally closed December 2025.

entity_name: Payten regional launch coverage in SEE tech/business press
source_name: Payten regional launch coverage in SEE tech/business press (PC Press, Biznis i Finansije)
why_relevant: Regional Serbian-language tech and business press carries detailed Payten product interviews (Android POS terminals, Live UTMS remote terminal management) that describe the terminal technology being rolled out across the group's markets including Montenegro. Useful for dating the technology generation of ME terminal estates when vendor PR is country-silent.

entity_name: PV Informer / Montenegrin online media reporting CBCG counterfeit data
source_name: PV Informer / Montenegrin online media reporting CBCG counterfeit data
why_relevant: Montenegrin outlets routinely restate CBCG counterfeit findings (most-counterfeited denominations, coins included) with more detail and earlier than the consolidated annual report. Serves as a discovery layer pointing back to the underlying CBCG release.
